Fed projections and market prices

Each FOMC participant submits a year-end rate they consider appropriate. The median can move between meetings, even when today’s target stays put. Market prices can already reflect part of that revision.

On 21 September 2022 the Fed raised its median end-2023 rate projection from 3.8% to 4.6%. One-year OIS rose 8.47 bp in the release window.

Inspect a Fed release and its market windows
Measurement, sources and Fed data

GDP and PCE inflation measure Q4 over Q4. The unemployment rate refers to the Q4 average. Published rate medians are rounded to one decimal place. One-year OIS spans a rolling year. Its horizon only approximately coincides with a December meeting’s following year-end projection. A change from the previous projection measures what the Fed revised. Measuring what investors expected before release requires a separate market price.

When euro-area inflation and growth diverged

ECB and Eurosystem staff prepare forecasts of annual-average inflation and real GDP growth. Follow how the projection for a particular year changed as successive vintages became available.

In June 2022, staff raised projected inflation for 2022 by 1.7 percentage points and lowered projected growth by 0.9 percentage points.

Inspect an ECB forecast vintage
Publication history, sources and ECB data

In early rounds the public projection could be a range. Each reading records whether it uses its midpoint, a published central forecast or a value recovered from the historical database. Public disclosure began in December 2000 with the June and December rounds. The ECB began publishing the March and September rounds in September 2004. The public filter therefore compares consecutive quarters only when both were public. Monthly vintage labels identify forecast rounds. An intraday market study also needs the time investors received the news.

Did official guidance and market prices move together?

A shift towards tighter policy means this text scored higher than the previous comparable document. The price change measures how much the market repriced during the communication window.
